programme.desc: Bella finds out all about some of the smallest mammals in the UK - mice! Chantelle visits a wildlife group to meet Sean, Mossy, Gabriela and Cara, and help them release harvest mice into the wild. Rory and his son Sandy are at a farm looking for mice. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain prehensile tails, where mice find food, how many babies they have and whether or not they hibernate. It’s also time to find out what mice do to help the planet! This episode’s Teeny Tiny Task is to make a tennis ball house for harvest mice.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Grandma comes to look after George and Freddie for the day and helps the boys make some special biscuits for Mum. There is extra excitement in store when it starts to snow. Will there be enough to build a snowman? Will Grandma brave the sledge? And what will mum think of those biscuits?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Je'nae is cooking her favourite meal of Jamaican saltfish and cabbage. Her family are Jamaican, and in Jamaica saltfish and cabbage is a very popular meal. Lots of people eat it for their breakfast, but Je'nae is cooking it as a very special dinner for her friends. She is using saltfish, fresh cabbage and colourful peppers in her meal. Je'nae's friends have mixed opinions about the taste of fresh green pepper. She hopes that they will like it cooked in her recipe. Her mum has cooked some tasty Jamaican dumplings and rice to eat with the fish, and Je'nae is really looking forward to seeing if her friends will like it as much as she does.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode Maddie is on the move. She finds out how things that we use every day are brought to us on big ships and moved around the country in shipping containers on trains. She visits a shipping port and uses a special camera attached to the shipping containers to find out what happens when they are lifted on a big crane. Next, Maddie visits a bubble packaging factory and uses a special slow-motion camera to show how the air gets trapped inside the bubble packaging when it is made.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Newfoundland Sylvie is a big therapy dog with big soft cuddles who loves to help people when they’re worried. She and her owner, Katrina, visit all sorts of people every day, young and old. Today, Sylvie and Katrina are visiting a doctor’s surgery to help a little boy called Ben. Ben has fallen off his scooter and grazed his knee, and his mum says he’s too nervous to come into the doctor’s room. Sylvie’s mission is to help Ben feel brave enough to see Dr Stevens. First, she gives Ben one of her biggest and best cuddles. Then, she and Dr Stevens show Ben how a doctor treats a patient. Sylvie loves performing in the starring role. Rafi makes a wish to freeze the café so they can read in peace. At first, it works, but frozen trams, floating crisps and silly surprises keep them busy. When the wish fades, Rafi helps Jake, and the café comes back to life with lots of giggles. Rafi decides the café is too noisy for reading, so she makes a cosy corner in her bedroom instead.

Gran Gran’s donating a special possession – the coat she wore as a child when she travelled from St Lucia to England. In the coat pocket, they find Gran Gran’s boarding ticket. There’s lots to see at the exhibition – one photo in particular catches Gran Gran’s eye. Jared is also visiting the exhibition and points out that it’s a photo of his grandad aboard a ship to England. JoJo spots a little girl in the photo wearing the same coat as Gran Gran. Gran Gran realises the little girl is herself! Now she has her coat, her ticket and a photo of her and Great Gran Gran travelling too.

Mother Clanger has heard that these amazing trees can sparkle and glow, but none of the Clangers know how this is done until, completely by accident, Tiny discovers that music is the answer.

programme.desc: The Squirrels are admiring everything Duggee has grown in his vegetable garden, especially his crop of giant carrots, when they hear a noise. They investigate and find the Rabbits busy preparing for the Carrot Solstice, the day when the sun is at its highest. On this day, they gather round Carrot Henge to celebrate the glory of this humble vegetable. Trouble is, the Rabbits need to go and get ready – but who will look after the carrots? The Squirrels volunteer, so off the Rabbits go. Looking after the carrots seems easy at first, and Norrie arranges tasks for everyone. Betty skillfully organises the queue while Roly is on toilet duty. And then, disaster strikes. Worm pops up and eats part of Carrot Henge. Duggee is dispatched to fetch one of his own giant carrots to fill the gap. As time ticks on with no Duggee in sight, the place gets busier, and the sun is nearly at the top. Will Duggee fix the Henge in time, or will Carrot Solstice be ruined?

programme.desc: Meet the really big square who always gets the party started: Sixteen! Learn all about the number 16 with Numberblock Sixteen.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!

The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos watch a potter make a pot on a wheel, and when he leaves the room, they come out to investigate. Chickedy and Chick jump inside the half-finished pot, while Great BigHoo presses the pedal down to make the wheel turn, and Toodloo starts to throw more clay onto the wheel. Great BigHoo gets carried away, making the wheel spin faster and faster, until the growing pot flails out of control and collapses in a heap! On the boat, the Twirlywoos try to have tea, but unfortunately the tea table is misbehaving. It spins around, sending Chickedy and Chick flying up into the air! Toodloo and Great BigHoo join in the fun and get spun up in the air too, before landing with a bump when the tea table disappears.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin spends the day with a monkey-loving friend, while Mr Tumble has fun playing hide-and-seek with the toys.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome little ones Oliver, Reau, Minnie, Theo, Francis and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Nigel has a toy umbrella inside his bag. All the parents and babies have different weather themed toys or objects too, which are explored through play, songs and a story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to hide a baby appropriate weather themed toy or object inside a fabric bag or pillowcase, to explore with their baby. Some viewers at home show how they’ve been discovering the weather too. The nursery rhyme I See Sunshine features, as does a story about Baby Bear cloud spotting. Plus, the Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with sensory lights and the Goodbye Song.

programme.desc: Lisa and the children create animal masks to pretend to be farm animals, learn signs for farm, old and pig, and sing and sign Old MacDonald Had a Farm.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Kipekee the elephant has fun as she discovers the talents of the other animals. Hamza sees some oryx in the wild and spends time with the baby zebras at the orphanage.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger releases baby Coconutdons into the jungle, realising they needed to be contained.

Chantelle visits a wildlife group to meet Sean, Mossy, Gabriela and Cara, and help them release harvest mice into the wild. Rory and his son Sandy are at a farm looking for mice. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain prehensile tails, where mice find food, how many babies they have and whether or not they hibernate. It’s also time to find out what mice do to help the planet! This episode’s Teeny Tiny Task is to make a tennis ball house for harvest mice.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Grandma comes to look after George and Freddie for the day and helps the boys make some special biscuits for Mum. There is extra excitement in store when it starts to snow. Will there be enough to build a snowman? Will Grandma brave the sledge? And what will mum think of those biscuits?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Je'nae is cooking her favourite meal of Jamaican saltfish and cabbage. Her family are Jamaican, and in Jamaica saltfish and cabbage is a very popular meal. Lots of people eat it for their breakfast, but Je'nae is cooking it as a very special dinner for her friends. She is using saltfish, fresh cabbage and colourful peppers in her meal. Je'nae's friends have mixed opinions about the taste of fresh green pepper. She hopes that they will like it cooked in her recipe. Her mum has cooked some tasty Jamaican dumplings and rice to eat with the fish, and Je'nae is really looking forward to seeing if her friends will like it as much as she does.

She visits a shipping port and uses a special camera attached to the shipping containers to find out what happens when they are lifted on a big crane. Next, Maddie visits a bubble packaging factory and uses a special slow-motion camera to show how the air gets trapped inside the bubble packaging when it is made.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Koa the tiger loves sweets, and his teeth hurt, but he doesn’t know why! A check-up reveals that he has bacteria in his mouth from all that sugar. Luckily, Vida knows just what to do. She teaches Koa to brush his teeth and to eat his beloved sweets as a treat instead of all the time.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Carrot is starring in her own circus and thinks that Supertato is trying to steal her limelight. She soon realises that Supertato is trying to rescue her from Evil Pea’s meddling.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy and the Ducklings come across a lost sheep and decide to look after it. When they get home, they argue over who gets to play games with their new friend.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: A mystery is afoot! Somebody’s been digging up and running off with Jackson’s giant vegetables. Detectives Mojo and Bo must follow the clues to the cagey culprit.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Dad is pretending to be an estate agent selling the Grannies’ house to Mum.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo find ways to entertain themselves on a family road trip.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Zog is too scared to fly after a bad crash landing, so Boom helps the doctors as their ambulance. Zog must overcome his fear and get back to the team.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Taran pretends his favourite teddy doesn’t belong to him, but when it goes missing, he gets upset. The Fantastics go on a bear hunt, and Taran realises he is not too old for teddies.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi and Finn want to read their adventure book at the Bake A Wish Café, but there are too many distractions - even Dash can’t focus! Rafi makes a wish to freeze the café so they can read in peace. At first, it works, but frozen trams, floating crisps and silly surprises keep them busy. When the wish fades, Rafi helps Jake, and the café comes back to life with lots of giggles. Rafi decides the café is too noisy for reading, so she makes a cosy corner in her bedroom instead.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran go to a special exhibition at the art gallery to learn about Gran Gran’s journey to England. Gran Gran’s donating a special possession – the coat she wore as a child when she travelled from St Lucia to England. In the coat pocket, they find Gran Gran’s boarding ticket. There’s lots to see at the exhibition – one photo in particular catches Gran Gran’s eye. Jared is also visiting the exhibition and points out that it’s a photo of his grandad aboard a ship to England. JoJo spots a little girl in the photo wearing the same coat as Gran Gran. Gran Gran realises the little girl is herself! Now she has her coat, her ticket and a photo of her and Great Gran Gran travelling too.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. The Shallots want to explore beyond the front garden, so Sarah comes up with a plan.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: As the air grows cold, a crystal-shaped seed lands on the Clangers' planet. Granny helps Tiny to plant it, and it quickly grows into a wonderful crystal tree. Other seeds fall, and soon there is a small forest of them. Mother Clanger has heard that these amazing trees can sparkle and glow, but none of the Clangers know how this is done until, completely by accident, Tiny discovers that music is the answer.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo takes care not to overfill a cup with water and teaches BaBa how to take sips from a very full drink. On the Play Tree, they fill containers with sand to make sandcastles. With the Yummies, they enjoy a delicious potato dish, which is very filling. As they sail on the Lullaby Lake, Elewhale fills the sky with twinkling stars. Gramma Leeba tells the friends about their very full day.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Pontipines count to five. Makka Pakka builds a pile of five stones. The Tombliboos are inside their bush, building with their own bricks. Each Tombliboo is building a tower, and when they begin to compare towers and share bricks, they succeed in building a very tall tower indeed, a tower of five. Everybody joins in the dance at the gazebo.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: New Zealand v Egypt
programme.desc: Live 2026 FIFA World Cup coverage from Vancouver as New Zealand take on Egypt. Mohamed Salah once again carries the hopes of a nation on the biggest stage in what could be his final World Cup. After missing out on the 2022 tournament in Qatar, Egypt returns with renewed belief and were held to a draw by Belgium in their opening match. New Zealand, meanwhile, are appearing in only their third World Cup and their first since 2010, when they left the tournament unbeaten but still exited at the group stage. Darren Bazeley's side twice they took the lead against IR Iran but couldn't seal what would have been a crucial win. They now face the much tougher test against one of Africa's strongest sides. Semra Hunter is joined by Jobi McAnuff and Ange Postecoglou. Commentary comes from Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: New Zealand v Egypt
programme.desc: Live 2026 FIFA World Cup coverage from Vancouver as New Zealand take on Egypt. Mohamed Salah once again carries the hopes of a nation on the biggest stage in what could be his final World Cup. After missing out on the 2022 tournament in Qatar, Egypt returns with renewed belief and were held to a draw by Belgium in their opening match. New Zealand, meanwhile, are appearing in only their third World Cup and their first since 2010, when they left the tournament unbeaten but still exited at the group stage. Darren Bazeley's side twice they took the lead against IR Iran but couldn't seal what would have been a crucial win. They now face the much tougher test against one of Africa's strongest sides. Semra Hunter is joined by Jobi McAnuff and Ange Postecoglou. Commentary comes from Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live 2026 FIFA World Cup coverage from Vancouver as New Zealand take on Egypt. Mohamed Salah once again carries the hopes of a nation on the biggest stage in what could be his final World Cup. After missing out on the 2022 tournament in Qatar, Egypt returns with renewed belief and were held to a draw by Belgium in their opening match. New Zealand, meanwhile, are appearing in only their third World Cup and their first since 2010, when they left the tournament unbeaten but still exited at the group stage. Darren Bazeley's side twice they took the lead against IR Iran but couldn't seal what would have been a crucial win. They now face the much tougher test against one of Africa's strongest sides. Semra Hunter is joined by Jobi McAnuff and Ange Postecoglou. Commentary comes from Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: New Zealand v Egypt
programme.desc: Live 2026 FIFA World Cup coverage from Vancouver as New Zealand take on Egypt. Mohamed Salah once again carries the hopes of a nation on the biggest stage in what could be his final World Cup. After missing out on the 2022 tournament in Qatar, Egypt returns with renewed belief and were held to a draw by Belgium in their opening match. New Zealand, meanwhile, are appearing in only their third World Cup and their first since 2010, when they left the tournament unbeaten but still exited at the group stage. Darren Bazeley's side twice they took the lead against IR Iran but couldn't seal what would have been a crucial win. They now face the much tougher test against one of Africa's strongest sides. Semra Hunter is joined by Jobi McAnuff and Ange Postecoglou. Commentary comes from Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.
